bib.title: Outrageously Large Neural Networks: The Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts Layer
bib.venue: Under review as a conference paper at ICLR 2017

question: Can conditional computation, via a sparsely-gated mixture-of-experts layer, raise model capacity by orders of magnitude with little loss in computational efficiency and improve language modeling and translation?
hypothesis: For larger training sets, even higher capacities would produce significant quality improvements.
contributions: A Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts layer with noisy top-k gating, trained jointly by back-propagation
Techniques for the shrinking batch problem and network bandwidth (mixed data and model parallelism, convolutional application)
Over 1000x capacity gains (up to 137B MoE parameters) with state-of-the-art results on 1B-word LM, WMT'14 En-Fr/En-De and multilingual MT

method.summary: A MoE layer (feed-forward experts plus a noisy top-k softmax gate) is inserted convolutionally between stacked LSTM layers (and in a modified GNMT). Trained with synchronous data plus model parallelism on 16-128 K40 GPUs, with importance and load losses for balance.

datasets.name: 1 Billion Word LM Benchmark (Chelba et al., 2013)
datasets.split: standard holdout set used for test perplexity

datasets.name: Google News 100B-word corpus
datasets.size: roughly 100 billion words (original 130B; neural models trained on max 100B)
datasets.source: Google internal news corpus, shuffled unique sentences

datasets.name: Multilingual 12 language pairs (Johnson et al., 2016)
datasets.source: same dataset as Johnson et al. 2016

models.name: MoE-4 ... MoE-4096-h (8M ops/timestep LM)
models.params: MoE layer 4M to 4303M; total 0.8-5.1B incl. embed/softmax
models.architecture: embedding, LSTM, MoE, LSTM, softmax; residual connections; dropout on layer outputs

other.expert: 1 ReLU hidden layer of 1024, output 512, about 1M params
other.gating: noisy top-k, k=4 flat, k=2 per level hierarchical

other.MoE-34M: LSTM 1024 units, hierarchical MoE 1024 experts, hidden 2048
other.MoE-143M: LSTM 4096 units with projection 1024, hierarchical MoE 256 experts, hidden 8192

models.name: MoE-GNMT (single pair)
models.architecture: GNMT with 3 encoder and 2 decoder LSTM layers (from 9 and 8), MoE after enc layer 2 and dec layer 1, attention

models.name: MoE-Multi
models.architecture: as single-pair, non-hierarchical MoE n=512, k=2, expert hidden 8192, noisy-top-k gating

training.objective: language modeling / translation cross-entropy plus L_importance and L_load (w * CV^2); softmax layer trained by importance sampling for LM
training.optimizer: Adam; 100B-word expert params use beta1=0 and factored second-moment estimate
training.lr_schedule: LM 1B: linear increase for first 1000 steps then proportional to inverse sqrt of step. MT: linear for first 2000 steps, constant for 8000 more, then inverse sqrt
training.batch_size: LM 1B: about 300,000 words; 100B-word: about 2.5 million words; MT: roughly 16000 words per GPU
training.epochs: 10 (1B-word LM); once-through on about 100B words (Google News)
training.tokens: about 100 billion words (Google News); about 3 billion sentence pairs (multilingual)
training.dropout: hyperparameter-searched DropProb in 0.1 increments for LM (0.1-0.4 in Table 7); 0.4 for single-pair MT
training.regularisation: w_importance=w_load=0.1 (1B LM), 0.01 (MT); Wg, Wnoise initialised to zeros
training.hardware: 16 K40 GPUs (1B LM), 32-128 K40 (100B LM), up to 64 K40 (MT), TensorFlow, synchronous
training.wall_clock: 1B LM 12-16 h (MoE-4 18 h); En-Fr 3 days/64 K40 (6 days longer); En-De 1 day/64 K40; multilingual 12 days/64 K40

other.memory_opts: expert hidden activations recomputed on backward pass; up to 1B params per GPU

inference.decoding: beam search as in Wu et al. 2016 (MT)

parameters.strictly_balanced_gating_inference: per-expert learned thresholds T replace batchwise mask

metrics.name: Test perplexity
metrics.definition: sum over all words incl. end-of-sentence symbol on holdout set

metrics.name: BLEU
metrics.definition: tokenized BLEU via multi-bleu.pl from Moses

metrics.name: TFLOPS/GPU
metrics.definition: FLOPs per training batch (incl. backward, softmax sampling, multiply-add counted as 2) divided by step time and GPU count

metrics.name: ops/timestep
metrics.definition: multiply-adds per training example per timestep, forward pass, excluding softmax

eval.protocol: single runs, no seeds or significance tests reported; test perplexity after 10 epochs for fair comparison with prior work

availability.data: 1B-word benchmark and WMT'14 public; Google News and Production data internal

evidence.quote: we limited training to 10 epochs, (27,000 steps)

results.claim: 65536-expert MoE (68B params) reaches 39% lower perplexity than the compute-matched baseline after 100B words.
results.setup: Google News 100B words, about 8M ops/timestep, MoE-65536-h vs 4xLSTM-512, 32-128 K40
results.quote: Perplexity after 100 billion training words is 39% lower for the 68-billion-parameter MoE

results.table: Table 8, row MoE-131072-h, column Test Perplexity .1 epochs
results.note: Table 8 columns are .1 epoch and 1 epoch; 1 epoch (100B words) values are 29.2 for 131072 vs 28.9 for 65536. Text says it 'degrades at 131072 experts, possibly a result of too much sparsity'

results.claim: MoE-4096-h with 4 active experts gets 24% lower perplexity than compute-matched baselines on 1B-word LM.
results.quote: the largest of the models (4096 experts) achieved an impressive 24% lower perplexity on the test set

results.claim: MoE-143M gets test perplexity 28.0 at 10 epochs versus 34.7 for best published LSTM.
results.table: Table 1, row High-Budget MoE Model, column Test Perplexity 10 epochs

results.claim: Low-budget MoE beats best published result while using 6% of computation.
results.quote: despite requiring only 6% of the computation

results.claim: MoE reaches 40.56 BLEU on WMT'14 En-Fr, +1.34 over GNMT+RL baseline.
results.setup: WMT'14 En-Fr newstest2014, 2048 experts, 6 days/64 K40, 85M ops/timestep
results.quote: Our approach achieved BLEU scores of 40.56 and 26.03 on the WMT’14 En→Fr and En→De benchmarks

results.claim: MoE reaches 26.03 BLEU on WMT'14 En-De, +1.12 over GNMT.
results.setup: WMT'14 En-De newstest2014, 2048 experts, 1 day/64 K40
results.table: Table 3, row MoE with 2048 Experts, column Test BLEU

results.claim: Multilingual MoE has 19% lower dev perplexity than multilingual GNMT.
results.setup: 12 language pairs, 8.7B params, 12 days/64 K40 vs GNMT-Multi 21 days/96 K20
results.table: Table 5, row Perplexity (dev), column MoE-Multi vs. GNMT-Multi
results.note: Text: 'The MoE model achieves 19% lower perplexity'

results.claim: Without balancing losses perplexity is 39.8 vs about 35.6 with them.
Computational efficiency stays at 0.72 TFLOPS/GPU at 65536 experts (99.994% layer sparsity).
results.note: Dense baselines ran at 1.07-1.29 TFLOPS/GPU; theoretical max 4.29

results.claim: Abstract claims greater than 1000x improvement in model capacity with only minor losses in computational efficiency.
results.setup: abstract headline claim; MoE layer up to 137B params vs dense LSTM baselines, GPU clusters
results.quote: achieving greater than 1000x improvements in model capacity

limits: Largest model (131072 experts) is inefficient at 0.30 TFLOPS/GPU because batch size was not scaled with GPU count
Quality degrades at 131072 experts, cause is conjectured ('possibly too much sparsity')
Diminishing returns beyond 1B MoE parameters on the 1B-word corpus
English-Korean MT worsens, attributed to oversampling of rare pairs
Trillion-parameter model on trillion-word corpus is a goal, not reached
Learning rate value, seeds and variance not reported; comparisons are single runs
MT experiments used strictly balanced gating from Appendix F due to infrastructure peculiarities since fixed
K40-era hardware and LSTM backbone; no transformer

terms.definition: the batchwise sum of the gate values for that expert
each expert receives a batch of approximately kb/n << b examples
